facts.text: IN: the order in which a MongoDB sharded cluster's components (balancer, config servers, shards, `mongos`, featureCompatibilityVersion) are upgraded or downgraded, and how the official order changed from 2.4 to 8.0. OUT: replica-set-only and standalone upgrade steps, FCV semantics in general, driver compatibility, SCCC→CSRS conversion mechanics, Atlas/Ops Manager automation, and the version-path rule (major-by-major). Those are separate frontier items.

In scope: the order in which the components of a MongoDB sharded cluster (balancer, config server replica set (CSRS), shard replica sets, `mongos` routers, feature compatibility version (FCV)) change binary version during an upgrade or downgrade; the rules that force that order; how the order changed across releases; and the limits of the procedure. Out of scope: standalone and replica-set-only upgrade paths, the version path between releases (which release you may jump to), driver compatibility, per-release compatibility changes, and Atlas or Ops Manager automation internals. 14. Binary order and FCV order are separate. The docs say to raise FCV only after all binaries, including `mongos`, are upgraded, and to run the command on a `mongos`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.0-upgrade-sharded-cluster.md 15. A `mongos` cannot connect to a `mongod` whose FCV is higher than its own. An old-binary `mongos` works against a new-binary cluster only while FCV stays at the old value. This makes "upgrade `mongos` before raising FCV" a hard requirement, not a preference. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.0-upgrade-sharded-cluster.md 16.
